To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the apoptosis index was closely associated with the proliferative marker MIB-1; and that the expression of the invasive marker PAI-1 was closely associated with histological grade, the proliferative marker C-erbB 2 and the proliferative marker Ki-67.
the immunohisochemical detection of PA1-1 in the stroma of DCIS is correlated with histological grade, and that the expression of MIB-1 is correlated with the apoptotic index in DCIS.

the immunohistological expression of the proliferating markers MIB- 1, C-erb B2 and the apoptosis index is related to histologic grading of the tumor and the expression of PAI1 in tumor cells and stromal tissue.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the biological markers of DCIS and their relationship to histological grade.
the biological behavior of DCIS and its relationship to histological grade.
the relationship between the immunohistochemistry of biological markers and the histological grade of DCIS.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the expression of PAI-I in the stroma of DCIS is associated with histological grade and with the expression of C-erbB-2 and Ki-67 in carcinoma cells.
the immunohistological expression of PAI1 in DCIS is closely related to histological differentiation and proliferation.

the invasive markers uPA, PA-1 and Cathepsins D are not related to the histologic grade of DCIS, but that PAI-1 and C-ErbB2 expression are related to the proliferative markers, and are therefore important in the pathogenesis of DCIS.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the expression of PAI-I in the tumor cells and stroma is related to the expression of the proliferating marker C-erbB-2 and MIB-1 in DCIS.
the immunohistological detection of the expression of urokinase plasminogen activation (uPA) and its inhibitor PAI-1 can be used as markers of invasive and proliferate factors for DCIS.
the expression of PAI1 in the cytoplasms of DCIS cells is associated with histological grade and proliferative activity.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the apoptotic index can reflect the biological behavior of DCIS.
the immunohistological detection of PAI1 is related to histologic grade and proliferative markers, and may play an important role in the pathogenesis of DCIS.
the immunohistopathological detection of PAI-I in the cytoplams of both carcinoma cells, and stromal cells, is related to histologic grade, and expression of proliferative markers Mib1, and C-erb2.
